A 54-year-old obese man is brought to the emergency department due to progressively worsening
shortness of breath over the past 8 hours. Two months ago, he was diagnosed with laryngeal cancer
after noticing a mass on the right side of his neck. He has a history of smoking two packs of cigarettes
daily for 27 years and consuming two pints of rum daily. On examination, he appears ill but is alert and
oriented to person, place, and time. His vital signs include a temperature of 37°C (98.6°F), pulse of
107/min, respiratory rate of 44/min, and blood pressure of 134/96 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air
shows an oxygen saturation of 89%. Physical examination reveals a 9-cm tender and firm subglottic
mass on the right side of the neck, cervical lymphadenopathy, labored breathing, and audible
inspiratory stridor, though he is able to answer questions. Lung auscultation is clear. Arterial blood gas
analysis on room air shows: | pH | 7.36 | |------|-------------| | PCO2 | 45 mm Hg | | PO2 | 74 mm Hg | |
HCO3-| 25 mEq/L | The patient has no advanced directive. What is the most appropriate next step in

management? Answer Choices: (A) Tracheal stenting (B) Cricothyroidotomy (C) Noninvasive positive
pressure ventilation (D) Bronchoscopy with mass biopsy (E) Needle decompression of the airway (F)
High-flow oxygen therapy (G) Tracheostomy (H) Endotracheal intubation (I) Surgical resection of the
mass (J) Oxygen supplementation via nasal cannula
 A. Oxygen supplementation via nasal cannula
B. Bronchoscopy with mass biopsy
C. Endotracheal intubation
D. Tracheostomy
E. Cricothyroidotomy
F. Needle decompression of the airway
G. Noninvasive positive pressure ventilation
H. Surgical resection of the mass
I. High-flow oxygen therapy
J. Tracheal stenting
